added_failures_note: derived as the set difference of the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite failure_ids; the response-budget parameter set differs only by which of its four variants the parallel run happened to fail, and the manifest's own serial control (mcp_base.log, mcp_head.log) fails all four variants at both revisions, so the node adds no real failure.

findings.text: the change teaches only one of the obligations view's two producers about queued rows. reckon/crew/obligations.py:1264 lists a queued row under run-queued, but the slice the sweep publishes, obligation_snapshot.payload_for, resolves a row's kind through _duty_kind (obligation_snapshot.py:1029) against CLASSIFICATION_DUTY_KINDS (obligations.py:48), which carries no 'queued' entry, so a queued row resolves to '' and is skipped. The snapshot the stop hook and prompt path read therefore omits the queued run while the direct derivation lists it, breaching the equality payload_for's own docstring states ('a slice and a derivation over the same files are equal field for field') and leaving the obligations view disagreeing with itself on the very pointer this node was dispatched to make consistent.

_NON_BLOCKING_KINDS mirrors obligations.py's vocabulary as {review-queued, unreadable-review-record} and does not carry 'run-queued', so _blocking_items (coordinator_obligations.py:1223) classifies the new duty as blocking. On the inline path (_stop -> _obligations_view()(project, session)) a coordinator holding a queued run is now held from stopping until the lane admits it, which is the wait the change's own comment at obligations.py:97-100 says the coordinator cannot shorten; at base the queued row was absent and blocked nothing, so this is a regression the change introduces.

the done_when requires the queued run be shown with its position and rank by crew(view=live) and reckon crew list; the only crew-list case is marked xfail (strict=False), so reckon crew list is unverified and reckon/crew_run_commands.py carries no position or rank. Three of the done_when's four surfaces are gated; the fourth is asserted only as expected-to-fail, so the node's done_when is not met as written.

the queued_placements docstring states 'position is its place among every queued request on the lane', but the lane parameter defaults to '' and both callers (obligations.py:1264, query.py:208) take the default, so the ordering spans every backend rather than one lane; the figure is consistent with the position runs.queue_dispatch reports (runs.py:619, also unnarrowed), so the behaviour is right and only the wording is wrong.
